indication.text: COSELA is indicated to decrease the incidence of chemotherapy-induced myelosuppression in adult patients when administered prior to a platinum/etoposide-containing regimen or topotecan-containing regimen for extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC).

citations.quote: COSELA is indicated to decrease the incidence of chemotherapy-induced myelosuppression in adult patients when administered prior to a platinum/etoposide-containing regimen or topotecan-containing regimen for extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC).

target_moa.text: Trilaciclib is an intravenously administered inhibitor of cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 (CDK4/6) that causes transient G1 cell cycle arrest of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells in the bone marrow, protecting them from chemotherapy-induced damage.

citations.quote: Trilaciclib is an intravenously (IV) administered inhibitor of cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 (CDK4/6) that appears to cause transient gap 1 phase (G1) cell cycle arrest of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) within the bone marrow
COSELA is a kinase inhibitor indicated to decrease the incidence of chemotherapy-induced myelosuppression in adult patients

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥10%) were fatigue, hypocalcemia, hypokalemia, hypophosphatemia, aspartate aminotransferase increased, headache, and pneumonia. Fatal adverse reactions occurred in 5% of patients (including pneumonia 2%, respiratory failure 2%). Injection-site reactions including phlebitis and thrombophlebitis occurred in 21% of patients.

citations.quote: The most common adverse reactions (\ge 10\% of patients with \ge 2\% difference in incidence compared to placebo) were fatigue, hypocalcemia, hypokalemia, hypophosphatemia, aspartate aminotransferase increased, headache, and pneumonia. (6.1)

Fatal adverse reactions were observed in 5% of patients receiving COSELA. Fatal adverse reactions for patients receiving COSELA included pneumonia (2%), respiratory failure (2%), acute respiratory failure (<1%), hemoptysis (<1%), and cerebrovascular accident (<1%).
Injection-site reactions including phlebitis and thrombophlebitis occurred in 56 (21%) of 272 patients receiving COSELA in clinical trials

requirement.text: 4018-1: Conduct a study in adult patients with ES-SCLC undergoing chemotherapy to evaluate the impact of trilaciclib on disease progression or survival in patients with chemotherapy-induced myelosuppression treated with a platinum/etoposide- or topotecan-containing regimen with at least 2 years of follow-up.

citations.quote: **4018-1** Conduct a study in a sufficient number of adult patients with extensive stage-small cell lung cancer undergoing chemotherapy to evaluate the impact of trilaciclib on disease progression or survival in patients with chemotherapy-induced myelosuppression treated with a platinum/etoposide-containing regimen or topotecan-containing regimen with at least 2 years of follow-up.

requirement.text: 4018-2: Conduct an in vitro metabolism study and CYP phenotyping study to determine the major metabolic pathway for trilaciclib and characterize the major circulating metabolite M8.

citations.quote: **4018-2** Conduct an *in vitro* metabolism study and CYP phenotyping study at clinically relevant concentrations to appropriately determine major metabolic pathway for trilaciclib. Characterize the formation of the major circulating metabolite of trilaciclib, M8, using the purified M8 compound with a validated bioanalytical method.

requirement.text: 4018-3: Conduct an in vitro drug-drug interaction study to evaluate the major circulating metabolite M8 as an inhibitor of major CYP enzymes and drug transporters.

citations.quote: **4018-3** Conduct an *in vitro* Drug-Drug Interaction (DDI) study to evaluate the major circulating metabolite of trilaciclib, M8, as an inhibitor for major CYP enzymes and drug transporters.
